summary: Read-only review complete: three remaining authorization/invalidation gaps. No edits, builds, tests, network access, or .env reads.

findings.title: Existing step-up consumers can use invalidated proof
findings.detail: The epoch-aware step-up requirement covers passkey management and password change but omits recovery-kit download and security-policy mutation. routes/admin-system.ts:206 and routes/admin-security.ts:214 still call the cached requireStepUp(admin). Pause either request after principal resolution, invalidate its step-up through passkey deletion or a credential change, then resume: the cached timestamp still authorizes disclosure of SELLRIGHT_MASTER_KEY or a policy change.
findings.fix: **Rule.** Every artifact row stores `epoch` = the owner's `security_epoch` when it was issued. Every use re-reads the owner row under the owner lock and requires `artifact.epoch = owner.security_epoch`; on mismatch the artifact is deleted (credentials: audited `passkey_invalidated`) and the request fails generically. In the new image, every step-up consumer requires a live calling session, fresh `step_up_at`, and `session.step_up_epoch = owner.security_epoch`, re-read under `admin_user FOR UPDATE` followed by the calling session `FOR UPDATE`; the cached principal is never sufficient. This includes passkey management, admin password change, `GET /v1/admin/system/recovery-kit`, and `PATCH /v1/admin/settings/security`. Hold these locks through the authorized operation: construct the recovery-kit result and record its download in the transaction, or acquire the store lock and commit the security-policy change and audit in that transaction. Use transaction-aware helpers on the same connection; do not call helpers that open another transaction while these locks are held. Preserve installation-admin, human, store-owner, absolute-expiry and idle-expiry checks. Native and passkey step-up both write `step_up_at` and `step_up_epoch` under the owner lock (§5); a NULL epoch requires a new step-up. Add deterministic real-route tests pausing both existing consumers after principal resolution, committing passkey deletion or credential invalidation, and then resuming: no recovery key is returned and no policy change or success audit is committed. Cover both lock interleavings without retries or sleeps.

findings.title: Staff invite acceptance still commits superseded identity proof
findings.detail: routes/admin-settings-advanced.ts:530-576 verifies an existing admin's password/factor or resolves their session before entering the acceptance transaction. It subsequently claims the invite and inserts membership without revalidating either proof. The new snapshot rules omit findAdminCredentialsByEmail and this caller, allowing acceptance after a TOTP epoch change, password replacement, or revocation of the authorizing session.
findings.fix:
Existing-account staff-invite acceptance (`admin-settings-advanced.ts` → `findAdminCredentialsByEmail`) is also restructured. The credential branch reads `security_epoch`, `password_hash` and the stored TOTP version together before password/factor verification and carries that snapshot into acceptance. Preserve the existing store-membership advisory lock first; then lock the existing `admin_user` row `FOR UPDATE`, require the same human identity and invite email, and require the captured epoch, password hash and stored TOTP version to match before claiming the invite or writing membership. Reject changed credential proof with 401 `INVITE_AUTH_FAILED`. The authenticated-session branch preserves CSRF validation and, after the owner lock, locks the exact authorizing session `FOR UPDATE` and revalidates its owner, absolute expiry and idle expiry; a cached `sessionHuman` result is insufficient. Keep invite claim, membership insertion and audit atomic, preserve the existing new-account and existing-membership guards, and perform no nested database calls while holding these locks. Add deterministic real-route tests pausing credential-based acceptance after verification across password replacement and TOTP disable/re-enable, and session-based acceptance after resolution across session revocation; rejection leaves the invite unconsumed and membership unchanged.

Deterministic concurrency controls (§8) race each new transaction against each row above and staff-invite acceptance in both orders.

findings.title: Native login rehash mutates state before snapshot validation
findings.detail: The revised login row checks epoch/TOTP only before session insertion while retaining the earlier conditional rehash. routes/admin.ts:82 invokes rehashAdminPasswordIfUnchanged, whose predicate checks only password_hash. A login paused after factor verification can therefore survive a TOTP cycle long enough to rehash the unchanged password and fire the new trigger, clearing freshly earned step-ups, before session creation rejects its stale epoch. A rejected stale-proof login still changes security state.
findings.fix: | Native admin login (`routes/admin.ts` → `createAdminSessionIfCredential`) | Password/factor verification and conditional rehash occur before the session-creation transaction; the rehash checks only the password hash | **restructured**: `findAdminByEmail` reads `security_epoch`, `password_hash` and the stored TOTP version together before password/factor verification. Compute any optional replacement hash outside the transaction, without writing it. In one mutation transaction, acquire `admin_user FOR UPDATE` and require the captured epoch, password hash and stored TOTP version to equal the locked row before any rehash or session insertion; reject a changed snapshot with the generic login failure. Only after this check may this request apply its verified rehash and insert the session, atomically. Remove the standalone pre-transaction rehash write from login. If SQL rehash remains best-effort, isolate it in a savepoint on this same connection so failure rolls back both the hash update and trigger effects before continuing with the unchanged hash. A boolean `secondFactorVerified` alone is insufficient. Add deterministic real-route tests pausing login after successful factor verification, disabling and re-enabling TOTP with both the same and a different secret, then resuming login and proving that no session is created. Include an outdated password hash and a fresh step-up earned after the TOTP cycle: the rejected login must leave both the password hash and all session step-up fields unchanged. |
